title: Indexed-tier pricing and rerank burst discount pilot
creator: Ava Chen
description: Run a bounded pilot that introduces an "indexed-tier" per-vector unit price for embeddings plus an explicit burst/volume discount for reranking workloads. Aim is to preserve predictable revenue while offering customers lower marginal cost when they batch or rerank at scale. This ticket scopes the experiment design, contract language updates for QSA/enterprise deals, billing prototype for the console, and the rollout checklist.
background: Customers building search and rerank pipelines report two pain points: 1) high marginal cost when doing batched embedding generation and rerank scoring; 2) unpredictable bills when synchronous rerank calls fan out to many vectors. Existing per-vector pilots focused on flat slab pricing and batch credits; this experiment tests a hybrid: a base per-vector index price (for storage/indexing and cold retrieval) plus explicit per-call compute units for rerank that get discounted when calls include >N vectors or when batched across time windows.
proposed_model: 1) Indexed-tier: base price per stored vector unit (per 1k vectors) for index/embedding storage and cold-kept KV. 2) Rerank compute units: per-rerank-call price expressed as per-vector compute units. 3) Burst discounts: tiered percentage discounts applied to rerank compute units when a single API call includes >= 100 vectors or when cumulative rerank vectors in a 60s window exceed 10k. 4) Pilot cap: enroll up to 12 customers for 90-day trial with opt-in SLA and usage telemetry access.
pricing_examples: Indexed-tier: $0.50 per 1k stored vectors / month (example bucket).
Rerank compute unit (baseline): $0.002 per vector evaluated in a rerank call.
Burst discount buckets: 10-99 vectors -> 10% off; 100-999 -> 30% off; >=1000 -> 50% off for that call or window.
Effective example: 2k-vector rerank call baseline cost = 2000 * $0.002 = $4.00; with >=1000 bucket discount cost = $2.00.
metrics: Primary revenue test: delta in ARPU for enrolled customers vs control over 90 days (target: <=5% downside).
Adoption: fraction of eligible customers who opt into the pilot (target >= 20%).
Unit economics: measured GPU-seconds per vector for rerank (target maintain within 10% of current baseline after batching).
Customer satisfaction: pre/post pilot NPS change for participants (target >= +5).
Billing predictability: reduction in bill variance month-over-month for batched rerank customers (target 30% decrease).
Fraud/abuse signal: increase in anomalous high-volume calls flagged (target: none beyond noise).
acceptance_criteria: Billing schema implemented in sandbox console and validated against historical usage within 5% error.
Telemetry dashboards show clear attribution of indexed vs rerank compute units.
Legal & QSA updates: contract amendment language and QSA checklist approved by security and legal.
Pilot cohort (>=6 customers) onboarded with billing opt-in and documentation.
Metrics collection pipeline instrumented and smoke-tested (latency, cost, error rates).
Rollout plan and rollback triggers documented (cost delta threshold, error spike threshold).
decisions: Use a hybrid 'index + compute' pricing model rather than replacing per-vector billing entirely.
Burst discounts will be evaluated on both per-call vector count and short time-window aggregated usage to support both single large calls and rapid small calls.
Start with a small cohort (12 customers) to limit revenue exposure and iterate contract language based on QSA feedback.
Expose detailed per-call cost breakdown in the Console Billing view for pilot customers.
No automatic downgrades of existing customers; pilot must be opt-in.

risk_and_mitigations: Revenue downside if high-volume customers see large discounts: mitigate by pilot cap, cohort selection, and ARPU guardrails in contract.
Complexity for billing implementation: mitigate by developing a sandbox prototype first and feature-flag rollout.
Customer confusion around billed components: mitigate by explicit console UI showing index vs rerank charges and sample invoices.
Security/classification concerns from QSA: mitigate by updating onboarding to require KMS config and adding audit log retention to pilot terms.
Abuse surface (clients trying to game discounts): mitigate by anomaly detection and rate-limit thresholds; include contractual anti-abuse clauses.
